Welcome to Echo Basin National Park

Where the mountains answer back

Echo Basin is 186,000 acres of glacier lake, old-growth cedar and high country, about two and a half hours from the city. We're open all year. Most people come for the lake. Almost everybody ends up yelling at the mountains from Echo Point, because they yell back.

Four landscapes, one park

Explore the park

  1. 8,560 ft

    Echo Pass

    Snow most of the year, and a warming hut that's staffed all summer.

  2. 6,230 ft

    Halloran Meadows

    Elk graze here most evenings, so bring binoculars and keep your distance.

  3. 4,270 ft

    Cathedral Stand

    Old-growth cedar and Douglas fir, some of it more than 600 years old.

  4. 3,540 ft

    Echo Lake

    Eleven miles long and cold enough to make you yelp.

Today in the park

The pass usually runs about 20 degrees colder than the lake, so check both temperatures before you pick a trail.
